title: The enriched API reproduces AvroSchemaFlattener's column names exactly, including the wrong ones
rationale: A migration guarantee consumers need, filed with its teeth showing. Agreement here is LOSSLESS in the mechanical sense and is bad news in the substantive sense: the new API inherits the legacy defect rather than fixing it. AvroSchemaFlattener.processFieldRecursively joins with a bare underscore and never escapes, which is exactly what EnrichedSchemaFlattener.join does under FAIL. Cross-reference avro-underscore-field-name-column-divergence, which records the same wrong answer for the legacy path.
catchesBugClass: Unilateral repair. The day someone fixes escaping in one flattener and not the other, this row goes red and names the drift - more useful than either flattener's own tests, since both would still pass in isolation.
cannotCatch: It is array-free, so it says nothing about the array-boundary divergence between the two: the legacy flattener joins array element fields with a single separator and the enriched one with the array-boundary marker. It cannot distinguish 'both correct' from 'both identically wrong'; only the MAP_FLATTENER row supplies that judgement.

predicted.detail: Both emit the same three unescaped names.

configDescription: assert ENRICHED_KEYSET vs LEGACY_AVRO_SCHEMA_FLATTENER, default FlattenOptions
